projects.name: Safarnama

award.title: Special Jury Award, Most Innovative Project
award.detail: ₹10,000 scholarship from the AEC Class 88′ Foundation

projects.summary: A travel platform built around responsible tourism, local discovery and a community of travellers. It started with my own solo trips and slowly grew into a much bigger product idea.

story.problem: Travel information is scattered across blogs, reels and random forums, and very little of it nudges people to travel responsibly.
story.idea: One traveller-first place that mixes discovery, eco-tourism and community, so planning a trip and caring about the place happen together.
story.solution: A single platform with guides, itineraries, a community forum, local food and events, safety tips, a carbon footprint calculator, an AI chatbot and an admin panel.
story.learned: Full-stack development end to end, thinking like a product person, UI/UX decisions, working in a team, and building around a real problem instead of a tutorial.

projects.name: WanderLink
projects.summary: A chat and community app for travellers. The idea is simple: the best travel tips come from people who were just there.

story.problem: On the road, the most useful information comes from other travellers, but there is no easy way to find and talk to them.
story.idea: A messaging app where travellers can meet around places and trips, from one-to-one chats to open communities.
story.solution: Planned: one-to-one and group chat, communities, public conversations and chat requests, plus the everyday controls (pin, mute, archive, favourites, block, clear) and media sharing.
story.learned: Designing real-time features and data models before writing code, and scoping. Not every feature has to exist on day one.

projects.name: This website
projects.summary: The site you are on. A hand-drawn 3D terrain on canvas, a live GitHub feed, and a hidden terminal. Built without a UI kit.

story.problem: Most portfolio templates could belong to anyone.
story.idea: Show the two things I actually do, building and travelling, in one visual language.
story.solution: React + Vite, a custom canvas terrain with no 3D library, plain CSS design tokens, and the GitHub public API.
story.learned: Performance budgets, accessibility, and how much restraint good design takes.
